name: Platformism
summary: Platformism is an anarchist-communist current that demands a tightly organised anarchist federation, built on shared theory, shared tactics and collective responsibility. It holds that class struggle and a violent social revolution must destroy the state and capitalism, with industry and land managed by workers' and peasants' bodies and goods shared by need. It rejects parliamentary democracy, any transitional state or party dictatorship, and the synthesis of competing anarchist tendencies.
scope: The classical platformism of the Dielo Trouda group (Arshinov, Makhno, Mett, Valevsky, Linsky) as set out in the 1926 Organisational Platform of the General Union of Anarchists (Draft), with its roots in the Makhnovist movement. It does not cover later developments such as especifismo or Fontenis's libertarian communism, nor the synthesist and individualist anarchist currents it opposed. Social questions the 1926 text never raised are inferred from its principles and marked low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not discussed; the Platform's communist distribution by need and equal provision implies free health care, but it would be organised by worker-peasant bodies rather than a state.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Platformists seek to abolish wage labour rather than reform it; a statutory minimum wage is a state reform that the Platform's rejection of reformist paths makes unattractive.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The constructive section replaces markets with planned production for need and exchange between town and country through worker-peasant co-operatives.

public-ownership.rationale: Industry is to be owned collectively by the producers and managed by soviets and factory committees, explicitly not by the state, so state ownership is rejected though common ownership is not.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxation presupposes a state that the Platform wants destroyed on day one; adherents want expropriation of capital rather than higher taxes within capitalism.

unions-good.rationale: The Platform treats revolutionary syndicalism as an instrument of class struggle that anarchists should join and guide, though it is a tool rather than the goal.

property-fundamental.rationale: Capitalist private property is to be expropriated and the means of production held in common by labour.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Adherents want capitalist firms abolished and expropriated, not regulated by a state, so tighter regulation is an inadequate reformist answer.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed directly; communist provision by need opposes cutting benefits, though the state-run welfare system itself is not endorsed.

worker-ownership.rationale: Industry is a single workshop of producers owned collectively and managed by workers' bodies, central to the constructive programme.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from hostility to state power and its apparatus, which anarchists see as an instrument of class domination.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed in the Platform; inferred from the anarchist rejection of state coercion, though the programme is silent and some adherents are puritanical.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; state-enforced speech law conflicts with the rejection of the state, although anarchists oppose bigotry socially.

strong-leader.rationale: The Platform rejects dictatorship and seizure of political power by any party or leader.

state-harmful.rationale: The state is an instrument of class domination that must be destroyed by the workers on the first day of victory.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; the Platform wants armed workers and a revolutionary army, so strict state gun limits are opposed, though no civilian policy is stated.

empower-police-military.rationale: The state's police and army are tools of class rule to be destroyed; the Platform's defence is a voluntary class army under workers' bodies.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The Platform is silent and adherents are split between legalisation and abolition of the exploitation involved.

decide-locally.rationale: Federalism is a core principle, with free agreement between local organisations, though the Platform also wants unified command and coordination in revolution.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the aim of a classless society without the state's punitive apparatus.

traditional-family.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the revolutionary transformation of social relations, though the text offers no family programme.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed in the Platform and it opposes state institutions like marriage law; the question does not map onto its programme.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the general libertarian left stance on bodily autonomy.

more-religion-public.rationale: Not addressed in detail, but classical anarchism is anti-clerical and the Platform seeks a secular, worker-run society.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; adherents oppose racial hierarchy as part of the class system but the Platform proposes no such programme.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed in the Platform; it predates the debate and adherents' views vary.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Platform is internationalist and class-based, and does not make national culture a goal.

gradual-change.rationale: The Platform insists that only violent social revolution can replace capitalism and rejects gradual reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from class internationalism and hostility to state border control; not addressed directly.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred from rejection of states; international bodies of states are not a Platform concern, while anarchist international federation is.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; the Platform opposes capitalist markets, but its own exchange is between producer co-operatives.

nation-first.rationale: The Platform speaks of the international working class, so national interest over global cooperation is alien to it.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from hostility to state militaries and their wars.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from class internationalism and abolition of states, which implies no state borders, but it is not stated.

limit-growth.rationale: The Platform is a productionist programme from the 1920s and does not address environmental limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; adherents would want worker-led action but the text is silent and rejects state-led remedies.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; neither endorsed nor rejected.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the text.

revolution-justified.rationale: The Platform's section on the necessity of a violent social revolution says there is no other way to transform capitalist society.

experts-over-public.rationale: The programme rests on self-management by workers and peasants under mass control, with the Platform criticising appointed managers.

central-planning.rationale: The Platform wants production run by workers' bodies federated from commune to federal level and criticises state-appointed management, though it plans production collectively.

socialized-markets.rationale: Markets are not endorsed; exchange is arranged between town and country by co-operatives, though worker ownership is central.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land is to be held by all working people and not bought, sold or rented, so a land tax within a market is irrelevant to it.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance of capital ends with expropriation; taxing it presupposes the state and private property that the Platform rejects.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; distribution is by need through collective provision, with priority for working families, not a state grant.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred; the Platform is internationalist and opposes state-run national economic policy.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Economic direction belongs to workers' soviets and factory committees, not the state, which is to be destroyed.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Land is held in common by the working people, and the peasants may farm on a family basis but without buying, selling or renting.

universal-morality.rationale: The Platform does not address moral philosophy and the question divides anarchists.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Platform says anarchism does not aim to seize political power or create a dictatorship, and rejects party rule of any kind.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hierarchical rule of any kind is rejected as class domination, and the state is to be destroyed.

democracy-best.rationale: The Platform calls democracy a variety of bourgeois dictatorship, in a section headed the negation of democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Parliamentary democracy is rejected, but how workers' bodies decide is described in terms of federal self-management rather than referenda.

workers-councils.rationale: The constructive section names workers' soviets and factory committees linked from commune to federal level as the basis of self-management.

right-to-secede.rationale: The national question is not addressed in the Platform, and federalism rests on free agreement, so adherents are unsettled on secession by regions.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rule by a few over others is the essence of the state that the Platform seeks to abolish.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Platform declares violent social revolution necessary and plans for years of civil war.

war-builds-character.rationale: The Platform treats war as a grim necessity of defending the revolution rather than a virtue.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred from abolition of the state; the Platform does not discuss religion, and abolition of the state makes a separation moot.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Platform's rejection of state authority and law as an instrument of class rule.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The Platform wants capitalism abolished, so privatised policing and defence would be an instrument of the owning class.

military-superiority.rationale: The Platform is internationalist and rejects state militaries, with defence entrusted to a voluntary class army.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Platform speaks of the international working class and does not frame society ethnically.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Platform's general part states that class struggle has been the principal factor shaping societies.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Distribution is by need with equal sharing of goods, so adherents favour economic equality, though they do not frame it as outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; adherents favour land held by working communities but the Platform does not consider indigenous peoples.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed by the Platform and adherents have no stated position.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from class internationalism, which organises across civilisation lines rather than uniting nations by culture.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The communist principle of from each according to ability, to each according to need, rests on solidarity and not self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Not addressed; the Platform demands collective responsibility within the organisation but the community-over-rights framing is not its own.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental questions are absent from the Platform.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; state population policy is contrary to anarchist principles.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The programme builds on industry as a collectively owned single workshop, so it is not anti-industrial.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed; the Platform neither pursues nor resists technological disruption.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from the demand for self-management by workers and peasants under mass control rather than rule by any apparatus.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from hostility to state surveillance.

restore-past-order.rationale: The Platform is a revolutionary programme seeking to overturn the existing order in favour of a new society.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The Platform insists on theoretical unity and consistency of action with professed principles, which is against pragmatic ideological indifference.

direct-action.rationale: The Platform rejects parliamentary democracy and says to prepare workers through class struggle and revolution, not electoral politics.

means-match-ends.rationale: The Platform defends organisational federalism and no coercion, but also accepts violent revolution and unified command, so the principle holds only in part.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The constructive section is built on industrial production run collectively.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The Platform has a unified workshop of producers but retains specialised industrial and agricultural roles, and does not call for abolition.

distribute-by-need.rationale: From each according to their ability, to each according to their needs is the stated distributive principle.

production-for-use.rationale: Production is to be organised by worker bodies for common provision, with exchange between town and country by co-operatives rather than for profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Platform's class analysis treats capitalism as the exploitation of labour by owners and calls for labour to manage economic life.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Platform rejects any transitional dictatorship, saying a transition period with state coercion is anti-anarchist in essence.

collective-farming.rationale: The Platform says peasants decide for themselves between communal and family farming, and promotes collective methods through propaganda but not pressure.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Class analysis implies war is driven by capitalism, but the Platform does not set out a theory of imperialism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Anarchists regard the state as illegitimate, but communist platformists do not treat taxation as theft in a property-rights sense.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; liberal state restrictions are not the framework of a stateless programme.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Platform stresses collective responsibility and collective organisation, though it also affirms members' independence.

conscription.rationale: The Platform prefers a voluntary revolutionary army to a conscripted state army.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred; the Platform relies on collective self-management and rejects the state, so the framing of leaving the country is foreign to it.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is an instrument of class domination to be abolished, and customers-and-exit logic is a capitalist one.

positive-liberty.rationale: The Platform's goal is the equality, freedom and independence of workers, including collective control of material resources.

media-academia-power.rationale: The Platform locates power in the class state and capital, not in media and universities.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not addressed; the Platform's class universalism contradicts racial hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: The Platform's own structures are soviets and committees, but it is not corporatist and opposes the state.

total-state.rationale: The Platform wants to destroy the state, and criticised the Bolshevik state-capitalist outcome.

national-rebirth.rationale: Inferred from class internationalism; national decadence plays no part.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The Platform is internationalist and anti-state, so imperial expansion is alien to it.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule by loyalty hierarchy is the kind of authority the Platform rejects.

bound-labor.rationale: Land is to be held by working people and not bought, sold or rented, so bound labour to a lord is rejected.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The Platform has no epistemology; some adherents accept ideology critique, others do not.

single-common-good.rationale: The Platform's class analysis holds interests are opposed between classes, so a single reasoned common good is not its premise.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Inferred from rejection of states and class internationalism; the Platform does not address Zionism.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed; adherents oppose state citizenship regimes but have no stated view on return rights.

revive-national-language.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and opposition to state-imposed culture; not addressed.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The constructive section has workers' soviets, factory committees and workers' management of works and factories.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; neither a state nor a market education scheme matches its aims.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy of a capitalist state is not a Platform concern.

economic-freedom.rationale: The Platform links freedom to collective ownership, not to market economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Platform's rejection of rulers and government.

national-self-determination.rationale: The national question is not addressed; the Platform organises by class and federation rather than national statehood.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred from hostility to state militaries and war.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Platform does not discuss epistemology and anarchists differ on reason and emotion.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from class internationalism; provision is by need.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Provision is by need with priority for children, the disabled and working families, but non-workers refusing production for counter-revolutionary reasons are excluded.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Platform bases itself on irreconcilable class struggle and rejects class partnership.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; revolutionary but not iconoclastic in its programme.

dominated-front.rationale: Inferred; the Platform's front is international working class, not states against Western powers.

workers-nation.rationale: The Platform's class is international and not defined nationally.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from equality of relations and rejection of hierarchy.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; capital itself is expropriated, so a ban on interest is moot.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Equality and abolition of the state's coercive hierarchies make legal racial segregation incompatible.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Platform says the state is an instrument of class domination.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from class internationalism; state-enforced cultural assimilation is opposed.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not addressed; a conspiracy theory of this sort conflicts with the Platform's class analysis.

proportional-representation.rationale: Parliamentary democracy is rejected as bourgeois dictatorship, so reform of parliamentary seat allocation is irrelevant.

national-mission.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and rejection of the state.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not addressed in the Platform; sympathy with equality but no stated analysis.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The Platform sees government as inherently an instrument of domination, though it frames this structurally rather than as corruption.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from opposition to state coercion.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; adherents want to dismantle the forces, not litigate them.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Any state is rejected, including a minimal one.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Platform's aim is equality of relations and freedom for all workers, though it does not discuss legal rights.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not addressed; the Platform anticipates a long civil war but no theory of socialism in one country.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The Platform abolishes the state, so civil codes are not its concern.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from rejection of state coercion and the Platform's silence.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; state religious bans are alien to it.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not addressed; secular outlook is typical of anarchism.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The Platform says the state must be destroyed on the first day and criticised the Bolshevik state-capitalist outcome.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Platform rejects democracy and the state, so consent is not how it sees authority.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist policy is not its concern and it opposes national economic competition.

population-transfer.rationale: Inferred from egalitarianism and opposition to state coercion.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The Platform says violent social revolution is necessary.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The Platform's communism rests on solidarity and the class struggle for common ownership.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; adherents reject the state's authority and would be the targets of such bans.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The Platform's critique of class domination is close to this, but it uses no republican framework.

separated-powers.rationale: The Platform aims to abolish the state, so checks between its branches are not something it addresses.

vanguard-party.rationale: Contested: the Platform wants a disciplined union to be the pioneer and theoretical mentor of the mass organisations, which Volin and other anarchists called a vanguard, but it rejects seizing power and any party dictatorship.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Scarce goods go first to children, the disabled and working families, and the programme serves the labouring classes.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed; housing is a collective matter and the principle is not spelled out.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes are tools of class struggle in revolutionary syndicalism and the Platform wants to guide it.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The Platform's analysis traces exploitation to class relations and not population.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no position on lotteries.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The Platform opposes state coercion, but it also expects revolutionary defence measures against counter-revolution, so it opposes state emergency powers.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The Platform has no price system, so price controls are not its concern.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Platform rejects party dictatorship and the state.

party-commands-army.rationale: The army is placed under the jurisdiction of worker and peasant organisations, not a party or a state.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and rejection of states.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed; anarchism rejects political office but would pay no extra privileges.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The union's members must carry out decisions reached jointly, and the Platform says there can be no decisions without their execution.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Not addressed; the Platform favours federation by free agreement but rejects states.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The Platform rejects the state and any one-person command over the revolution.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; hierarchical authority is rejected.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by any authority over others is rejected.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Inferred from class internationalism; the Platform does not address the question directly.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; state censorship conflicts with the Platform's aims.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Leaders and offices of the state are rejected, so unlimited tenure is rejected.

recall-officials.rationale: Management by soviets and committees under mass control suggests accountability, though recall is not specified.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Inferred from rejection of state militaries and their alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Rent is abolished along with private property, but not through compulsory ownership by families.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Platform's defence is a voluntary revolutionary class army under worker and peasant organisations, not a professional state army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Platform lays equal stress on emancipating workers and peasants and does not romanticise the countryside.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The national question is not addressed; the Platform is internationalist.

death-penalty.rationale: The Platform rejects state punishment as class rule, though it does not address capital punishment.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; a modern issue consistent with the libertarian left.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the secular outlook typical of anarchism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; state restrictions on adults conflict with its principles.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from rejection of states and national exclusion.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from federalist free association.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; the state laws involved are rejected.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Platform's stress on freedom and independence.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred from anti-capitalism; the Platform does not address international debt.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Platform stresses that political change without expropriation leaves class rule intact.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The Platform denounces democracy as bourgeois dictatorship and wants the workers' soviets rather than an assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The Platform criticised the Bolshevik dictatorship and rejects restricting freedom in the name of the transition.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not addressed; state aid is not a Platform concern.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from hostility to state militaries.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state is not wanted in any form, so its election is irrelevant.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not addressed; central banks are state institutions of the capitalist order.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from rejection of national territorial claims.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property in the means of production is to be common, and land cannot be bought, sold or rented.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Platform's authors described the outcome of the Russian Revolution as state capitalism and a Bolshevik party dictatorship.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from rejection of state military alliances.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Rejects the state as authority and religion is not discussed.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: No head of state is wanted.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from rejection of state coercion and federalism by free agreement.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Rulers and their authority are rejected.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; taxation within capitalism is not its concern.

character-from-environment.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the belief that class relations shape society.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Platform rejects the ruler and the state, and a ruler unbound by law is the opposite of its self-management.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is absent from the 1926 text and adherents hold no common view, so this is a neutral inference.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred from the aim of abolishing the state; the Platform does not discuss constitutions.

leader-cult.rationale: The Platform rejects dictatorship and rulers.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family custody law is not addressed by the Platform, and adherents have no shared view on court presumptions.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The Platform criticises Bolshevik party rule as state capitalism, and sees leaders restoring domination.

land-redistribution.rationale: The constructive section says land is redistributed by working peasants and rural wage earners and belongs to all working people.

refugee-return.rationale: The Platform never discusses refugees or return rights, and its stateless outlook gives no clear direction either way.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from rejection of state coercion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from rejection of state coercion.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed; money and markets are not its tools.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; the national question is absent.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The Platform takes no position on minority strategy between emigration and local rights, as it works by class rather than nation.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Inferred from the Platform's view of class struggle as the main force shaping societies; it does not set out a materialist theory of history.

ban-cartels.rationale: The Platform seeks abolition of capitalism rather than competition policy.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; capitalist firms and banks are to be expropriated.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Rejects both democracy and state courts.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Not addressed; the Platform does not endorse state quotas.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Treaties between states are not a Platform concern, and adherents would see such standards as reformist and state-made.

moral-incentives.rationale: Communist distribution by need rather than work implies non-material motives, though the Platform does not discuss it.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Platform wants mass preparation by organised anarchists among workers and peasants, not a small armed group substituting for them.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Class privilege is to be abolished, including hereditary advantage.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Platform rejects rule of some by others.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Platform is class internationalist and anti-state.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Admissions and hiring policy is not addressed by the 1926 text, and adherents are divided on state-run preference schemes.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed; a state body issuing money is a state function.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The Platform expects capitalism to be replaced by violent revolution and not to reform its way out.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from rejection of states and imperialism.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The Platform treats workers as one class with a shared interest.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not addressed; private property rights as a defence for discrimination are not accepted.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The state and its legal constitution are to be abolished.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The Platform never discusses colonial treaties, so no stance can be drawn beyond general hostility to states.

elective-rulers.rationale: Rulers are rejected altogether, whether elected or inherited, and democracy is called bourgeois dictatorship.

minority-veto.rationale: The Platform requires members to carry out joint decisions, saying there can be no decisions without their execution.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Rulers may be overthrown, but the Platform rejects rule altogether, so the premise differs.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Platform calls parliamentary democracy bourgeois dictatorship.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics are absent from the Platform and anarchist communists of the period had no common stance.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The Platform says nothing on animal use, and adherents lack any shared view on food and research.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The Platform expects workers' self-emancipation, not paternalism by the rich.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The Platform is an organising programme demanding active participation.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The Platform has no theory of mass culture, and it locates domination in state and capital rather than media.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The Platform stresses state coercion and class domination and does not discuss hegemony.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory postdates the Platform, which gives no analysis of unequal exchange between poor and rich countries.

party-own-road.rationale: Not addressed, though it criticises Bolshevik dictatorship.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy for poor countries is not addressed, and the Platform's internationalism gives no clear answer.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; rejects political rule by any group.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitutions are state instruments the Platform rejects.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The Platform attacked Bolshevik dictatorship but did not equate it with fascism.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Public memorials are not discussed by the Platform and adherents have no shared position.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The 1926 text gives no analysis of gender disadvantage, so adherents have no settled position.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is not addressed by the Platform and no shared adherent view exists.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The Platform proposes a universal class revolution.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army is subordinate to worker and peasant bodies, and the state is to be destroyed.

paid-care-work.rationale: Unpaid care work is not treated in the Platform, and abolishing wages makes the question awkward to frame.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from anti-traditional hierarchy.

office-by-exam.rationale: The state apparatus is abolished and the Platform criticises appointed officials.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Federalism with self-management under mass control suggests delegates accountable to those who chose them, though the Platform stresses binding decisions more.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land belongs to all working people and cannot be bought, sold or rented, so holding is by use.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliaments are rejected, so budget approval by them is irrelevant.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land belongs to the working people and the national angle is absent.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anti-discrimination doctrine is absent from the Platform and adherents are split on state legal tests.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The Platform is a productionist programme that does not criticise consumption or status goods.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from rejection of state action, though support for revolutions abroad is possible.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from rejection of state imperialism and the Platform's criticism of Bolshevik domination.

corporate-influence.rationale: The Platform sees capital as dominant, and state and capital as aligned.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Anarchist communism ends wage labour with distribution by need, though the Platform does not explicitly demand abolishing money.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The Platform abolishes the state and capital but rejects market-led money, so it neither fits this statement nor opposes the abolition.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised class partnership bodies contradict the Platform's rejection of the state and of class collaboration.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred: anarchist-communists oppose state control of civil society and the press, though they scarcely address foreign funding.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from rejection of state policy and the state's role in family life; not addressed in the Platform.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: it calls for abolishing private property and communal management, not local state restrictions on purchase.

job-guarantee.rationale: It seeks to abolish wage labour and the state, so a state employer of last resort contradicts it; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: It rejects parliamentary democracy as a form of class rule and holds peace follows only from revolution; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: It holds that the state is an instrument of class domination to be destroyed, so no law binds merely as law.

non-intervention.rationale: Internationalist class solidarity and support for revolution abroad conflict with an absolute bar on outside involvement; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: The Platform has revolutionary syndicalism and workers' organisations by industry managing production, but takes no explicit stand against craft unions.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Its analysis is class-based and internationalist, so minority conspiracy claims contradict it.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from abolition of the state and its property law; the Platform does not discuss marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred: it opposes state secrecy and wants collective management open to the workers, but not a state transparency law.

local-production.rationale: It plans a federated, communist economy managed by workers' and peasants' bodies without clear localism.

informal-organisation.rationale: It explicitly demands a tightly organised federation with collective responsibility and rejects loose, unorganised groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: It rejects states and their constitutions, so no national supremacy; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: It is internationalist, anti-state and class-based, rejecting nationhood defined by religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of the state and of hierarchy; communities should relate as equals through federation.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from distribution by need and a federation of workers' and peasants' bodies, which pool resources rather than keep regional revenue.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Platform puts production and land under workers' and peasants' bodies and distribution by need; ordinary personal possessions are not targeted, so this is inferred for them.

defeat-communism.rationale: As anarchist communists the Platform's authors oppose defeating communism as such, though they fought Bolshevik state power; inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The Constructive Section gives production and distribution to workers' and peasants' bodies, with no private or mixed providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Platform does not discuss religion; inferred from the anarchist tradition and its materialist class analysis.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred from the Platform's class analysis, which treats capitalism as concentrating production and creating the base for communism; it is not stated directly.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from its call for abolishing class society and wage labour; the 1926 text does not address women's equality.

socialized-care.rationale: Not discussed; communal distribution by need implies shared domestic services, inferred from that principle.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from its internationalism and rejection of nationalism and state authority over culture.

treaties-binding.rationale: The Platform rejects the state altogether, so treaties with a government do not fit its framework; inferred as neutral.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Its federation of self-managed workers' and peasants' bodies with common property resembles this, though it is organised around industry and soviets, not small communities.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from its internationalism and opposition to state-led national projects.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Platform seeks anarchist communism and rejects both capitalism and a communist party-state, but it calls itself communist, so the answer is inferred and ambiguous.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Platformism rejects nationalism and holds that land belongs to the workers who work it; inferred from its internationalist class politics.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Platformism is an anti-fascist, class-based anarchist current opposed to antisemitism; the Platform does not discuss the Holocaust, so this is inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not discussed in the 1926 text; anarchist opposition to state coercion implies disagreement, but it is inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Platform rejects any state or party dictatorship and holds that workers organise freely in their own federations, so state suppression of opposition is rejected; it does demand revolutionary force against the counter-revolution.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The General Part rejects religion alongside the state as tools of exploitation, so it would not punish dissent; the Platform does not mention blasphemy law directly.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Platform is anti-colonial and anti-imperialist in its class analysis; the General Part denounces imperialist exploitation.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; it supports the armed resistance of the workers against oppressors but is secular and rejects religious duty. Inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: It calls for violent social revolution against states, but not on religious grounds; it rejects religious law as a basis for authority. Inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Constructive Section vests the running of industry and land in workers' and peasants' organisations, soviets-like councils and federations without a state, which is direct participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The Platform grounds its analysis in class struggle and is silent on race and sex.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed in 1926; anarchist principles of equal freedom suggest support but the text is silent, and adherents are split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The Platform rejects synthesis and demands a sharply defined class position; the General Part dismisses 'above class' politics.

alienated-labor.rationale: The General Part describes wage labour as exploitation of the worker by capital and the state, but it uses Bakuninist class analysis more than the vocabulary of alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is secular and internationalist, so it would not consider any religion incompatible with a culture. Inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Platform rejects the state and religion and holds that authority comes from the workers' own federations; the General Part treats religion as a prop of the ruling classes.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Platformism is secular and anti-clerical, so inferred support for excluding religious dress, but the 1926 text does not discuss state institutions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as neutral because a platformist society would not rest on employer contracts, but it would not use courts either.

social-market-economy.rationale: The Platform rejects both capitalism and state-run economy and calls for production managed by workers' bodies, so a regulated market is not its goal.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Not addressed; it rejects the standing army of the state but defends the revolution's own armed force of workers, so abolition applies to state armies. Inferred.

rich-first.rationale: Its principle of communism, distribution by need and equality of production, runs against letting some grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not addressed; the internationalist class position opposes both capitalist blocs but the 1926 text does not frame this.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Platformism aims to abolish the state and every hierarchy, so hereditary office is rejected.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: the Platform wants goods shared by need through workers' bodies, not credit issued by banks of any kind.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Not addressed; it rejects the state and capitalism wholesale, so a government's stance toward lenders is outside its frame.

property-franchise.rationale: The Platform rejects parliamentary democracy and class rule, and a property qualification for voting is the opposite of its aims.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not addressed in 1926; no stance on domination of nature or gender is stated.

reification.rationale: Inferred from its class analysis that capital rules workers; it does not use the term.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred: the Platform holds that bourgeois freedoms are hollow for workers who lack means.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred: it rejects state courts and laws as class instruments, so rulers governing by any law is not its model.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Platform is built on class solidarity across peoples and has no ethnic criterion for rights.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic: the 1926 text predates the internet and does not address it.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic: not addressed; it rejects the state whose records would be opened.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred: the movement is anti-clerical and egalitarian and would reject legal restrictions on who may marry.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from its class-based internationalism, which opposes discrimination against minority groups.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: the Platform rejects parliamentary and representative forms and wants decisions made by federated workers' and peasants' bodies, not mixed assemblies of citizens chosen by lot; it never addresses sortition.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred: Platformists were militantly atheist and saw religion as a tool of ruling classes, so they would not support reforming it; the Platform does not discuss the matter.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Platform holds that capitalism's concentration of wealth and the state it sustains must be destroyed and replaced by communal ownership.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The Platform never addressed this; its demand for equality and abolition of class privilege implies no one should be excluded, inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Platform seeks to abolish the state and does not envisage state education promoting any belief; inferred from its anti-statism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The Platform would abolish the state and its coercive organs, but it also provides for armed defence of the revolution, so this is inferred and tempered.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The Platform rejects any state or party holding power; guaranteed governmental shares for communities presuppose a state; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The Platform sees worker and peasant bodies providing distribution by need as of right, not charity; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: The Platform rejects parliaments and elected office, so term limits for politicians do not arise; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: The Platform favours federated worker and peasant bodies with collective responsibility and discipline over individual delegable voting; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed by the 1926 text and its principles give no clear direction.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The Platform calls for abolition of class and caste privilege, but did not discuss religious office; inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Platform did not discuss marriage; its egalitarian aims imply shared authority, inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not discussed; the Platform bases society on workers' and peasants' bodies open to all who labour, so excluding foreign workers from local voting would cut against its class internationalism. Inferred.

rent-control.rationale: The Platform abolishes landlord ownership and distributes goods by need in a communist order, so a state-imposed cap is not its method; adherents would meet the problem by revolution, not regulation. Inferred.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not discussed. Anarchist communism rejects private property in the means of production, yet the Platform says nothing about intellectual property specifically.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Platform rejects the state and militarism of the nation; it provides only a voluntary revolutionary army under workers' control, not drilled national-service youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The Platform opposes states and their armies, and nuclear arms would be incompatible with its voluntary workers' defence; the text does not mention them. Inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The Platform rejects the state and every government's standing army, so foreign bases would be instruments of state power the revolution should destroy.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not discussed; the Platform rejects governments as the arbiters of justice, so formal state recognition is outside its terms, though it would condemn mass killings. Inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Platform abolishes the exploitation of labour by owners and has goods distributed by need and production run by workers' bodies, so income cannot derive from ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The Platform demands a violent social revolution and a voluntary revolutionary army, so it accepts killing in defence of the revolution; adherents would not hold an absolute ban.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Platform is internationalist and class-based and rejects the nation-state; a claim of national continuity from ancient origins is foreign to it.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not discussed; the 1926 text never raises sex or gender, and the question is a modern theoretical one. Left neutral.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not discussed; the Platform organises by class, not by gender category. Inferred neutral.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Platform rejects the state and nationalism and the honouring of martyrs as saints is religious language alien to its materialist revolutionary stance.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Platform grounds politics in class struggle and material conditions, not a spiritual struggle between good and evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not discussed; the Platform is internationalist and the question concerns diaspora homelands. Inferred neutral.

culture-before-state.rationale: The Platform puts class struggle and social revolution first and treats the state as something to destroy, not a stage after a cultural renewal.

god-not-male.rationale: Not discussed; the Platform is materialist and rejects religion, so it would not describe God at all. Inferred neutral.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: The Platform is materialist and does not test religion by any standard; it would regard religious texts as irrelevant or oppressive. Inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The Platform seeks workers' and peasants' control across class lines and rejects nationalism, so giving a national majority the economy opposes it.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The Platform rejects nation-based territorial units in favour of a federation of workers' bodies. Inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: Unions and mass bodies are class organs of the workers; the Platform rejects any state or party control over them.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The Platform puts production in the hands of workers' and peasants' bodies and rejects a party dictatorship or transitional state.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred: industry is socialised and managed by worker bodies for the whole community, so essentials stay common, but not as state property.

second-chamber.rationale: The Platform rejects parliamentary democracy and legislatures altogether in favour of workers' self-management.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: production is run by federated workers' and factory bodies, not by the local community as such.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The Platform sets out a federalist structure with executive bodies that carry out and coordinate, while rank-and-file bodies decide.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred: the Platform aims to abolish wage labour and distribute by need, so a wage-level demand is a reformist goal.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not discussed; nothing in the Platform bears on drug regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from communist distribution by need and production for the common good.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from hostility to state control and surveillance.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from hostility to state control and surveillance.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred: anarchists reject the state but the Platform demands collective responsibility that binds members, so adherents would not endorse this wording.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Inferred: the Platform rests on materialist class analysis and says nothing of spiritual needs.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The Platform builds federation from the bottom up; there is no national legislature to grant or withdraw powers.

gm-crops.rationale: Not discussed; no basis in the Platform for a position.

dense-cities.rationale: Not discussed; no basis in the Platform for a position.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The Platform treats class, not race, as the line of political interest and struggle.

racial-pride.rationale: Not discussed; inferred class-first internationalism neither endorses nor condemns this.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred: the Platform opposes state armies and wants a voluntary revolutionary army to defend the revolution, which fits neither side of this statement.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The Platform is class-based and internationalist, treating nations as less basic than class; a language-defined nation is not part of its programme, inferred.

communal-electorates.rationale: The Platform rejects the state and any separate representative bodies in favour of class organs of workers and peasants, so religious electorates are alien to it.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Platformists see states and capital, not foreign powers, as the enemy, and treat nationalist plot claims as a distraction from class struggle; inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Not discussed; the Platform's communist distribution by need and workers' management of society implies free education, but organised without a state.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental taxes are state measures that the Platform's rejection of reformism and of the state makes unattractive; the 1926 text never raised the issue, inferred.

future-generations.rationale: The 1926 text did not raise ecology; inferred from its aim of a society managed for the common good, low confidence.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The Platform treats class, not sex, as the basis of political interest and never singles out women's values; inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: The Platform calls for arming the revolution and a revolutionary army defending the gains against counter-revolution, so general disarmament is not its aim.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Platformists reject state secret treaties and diplomacy as bourgeois instruments, but the text does not address diplomacy directly; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: Capital controls would be a state measure; the Platform seeks expropriation of capital by workers' bodies rather than state management of its movement, inferred.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Platform wants the state and its coercive apparatus destroyed and replaced by a voluntary revolutionary army answerable to workers' and peasants' bodies, so a permanent state monopoly on arms contradicts it.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from its anarchist rejection of state authority and its view that wars between states serve ruling classes; it prefers turning conflict into class war, not mere refusal.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: the Platform treats unions as tools for revolutionary struggle and aims to abolish wage labour, so bargaining with employers is at best a limited tactic.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: a state-run top-up that leaves capitalism and wage labour in place is a reformist palliative the Platform would not champion.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: it would abolish the state and capitalism, so legal limits on state borrowing are beside the point and tie it to the existing order.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred: it seeks the overthrow of capitalism worldwide, not a rewriting of the rules of the international economy by states.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The General Part says the state must be destroyed by social revolution and rejects any transitional state or party dictatorship.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The Constructive Section sets out a definite economic order of workers' management and distribution by need, though it leaves details to the workers' bodies.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: pricing nature as capital extends market logic that the Platform wants abolished along with capitalism.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Platform frames society by class and internationalist revolution, with no place for a sacred national community.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred: it would abolish debt-based schooling and give education freely under workers' bodies, but the text never addresses student loans.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The Platform analyses exploitation by class, not by region, and never discusses internal colonialism; adherents could read it either way.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The Platform does not address human nature; adherents draw on mutual-aid ideas while also wanting a transformed society.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: it would have workers' bodies run any media, and state funding sits badly with its rejection of the state.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Not discussed; the Platform's materialist, class-based programme leaves no place for a shared spiritual truth, so adherents are inferred to treat religion as an obstacle rather than a truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Not discussed; the Platform has workers' and peasants' bodies manage land and exchange themselves and rejects the state, so state price guarantees are inferred to be refused, though cooperative credit would fit.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Not discussed; the Platform aims to abolish the state and its armed forces, so keeping state arsenals is inferred to be opposed.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Platform rejects parliamentary politics and any workers' political party seeking state power, and wants class organisation through unions and an anarchist federation instead.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the Platform's commitment to equality and opposition to coercive custom, though it would rely on revolutionary social bodies rather than state law.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the Platform's equality of all producers and abolition of private property, which would end inheritance of land by anyone.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not discussed; the Platform has no language policy, and nothing in its principles settles whether regional names make separate languages.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Not discussed; the Platform rejects state courts and law, but it also holds property collectively, so private tort suits are inferred to be disfavoured.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the Platform's rejection of all hierarchy and authority, which excludes any official body of traditional leaders.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not discussed; the Platform's emphasis on free producers and abolishing coercive authority makes subordinating liberty to an imposed priority unlikely, though collective management could restrain harm.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the Platform's rejection of the state's courts and punitive justice, which fixed legal sentences would extend.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the Platform's opposition to state compulsion and its internationalist outlook.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The Platform treats unions as tools of class struggle and says nothing about membership rules; adherents' views are not stated.

voter-id.rationale: Platformists reject parliamentary elections altogether and so would not endorse state gatekeeping of voting; inferred.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Platform is silent on religion's legal status; it rejects the state altogether, so the question hardly arises.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The Platform rejects parliamentary democracy as a form of bourgeois rule that cannot serve workers.

premarital-sex.rationale: The 1926 text never raised the question; acceptance is inferred from the anarchist rejection of state and church regulation of private life.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Platform's rejection of state coercion and its aim to abolish the state's power.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The Platform demands the abolition of the state and wage system, with goods distributed by need, not a state cash scheme.

women-suffrage.rationale: Platformists reject electoral voting and office, so the vote is not valued, while they hold that all workers are equal; split and unaddressed.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The Platform does not discuss women's oppression or religion's role in it.

race-social-construct.rationale: The 1926 Platform does not address race, and the sources give nothing to infer from.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Dedicated state agencies run against the Platform's rejection of the state; inferred from that principle.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the Constructive Section puts land and industry under workers' and peasants' bodies, so individual claims by first use are not the basis of ownership.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred: the Platform rejects state institutions, so adherents would distrust state-run courts, though it does not mention them.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred: it is a revolutionary anarchist-communist programme with no religious basis, and anarchists oppose religious authority.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred: it demands the full equality of all workers, but the Platform does not discuss gender or self-government arrangements.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: the Platform calls for destroying the state and rejects any post-revolutionary state power, including a bureaucratic planned state.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: it rejects parliaments but organises through federated delegates, so adherents could fit either side.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred: it demands the destruction of the state and offers no role for churches in public life.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: its federalism lets local communities and peasants' bodies manage their own affairs, though minority regions are not discussed.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred: the Platform does not discuss disputed territory.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: it aims to abolish states, so state borders are not a theme.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred: the Constructive Section looks to organised industrial production and goods shared by need, not a return to simple living.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the Platform does not address indigenous settlement.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: anarchists oppose state conscription, which fits the 'neither' option, though no source states it.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: As an internationalist anarchist-communist current it rejects national loyalty and the state, so a national duty to the land is not part of it.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred: it rejects the state's monopoly of force, though the Makhnovists executed enemies in war.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred from its anti-state internationalism; it would not align a state with any great power.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: It is internationalist and anti-state; a state backing its 'nation' abroad contradicts that.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The Platform's constructive section places land and industry in common ownership of workers' and peasants' bodies.

self-ownership.rationale: The Platform stresses collective responsibility, and individual self-ownership is not discussed; inferred.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred from its concern for workers and peasants; the Platform does not address taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred: goods are shared by need and provision is universal, not means-tested.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: It rejects dictatorship and leader-based rule and wants federated organisation, though not discussed directly.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to capitalism and the state.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from its anti-clerical, class-based politics; not discussed in the Platform.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred: it looks to revolution and workers' management rather than ancestral values.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from its libertarian-communist principles; the 1926 text never raised it.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred: it wants workers' bodies, not a national state, to manage resources.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Distribution by need and common ownership of production mean fairness is judged by outcome, and private fortunes from exchange are exploitation.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not discussed; a state-collected levy sits poorly with a stateless programme, though a hostile view of finance and capital is implied.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the Platform's class analysis that sees exploitation, not race, as the central division and that would not call oppression solved.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the Platform's rejection of the state's authority and of legality as a limit on revolution, though the natural-law framing is foreign to it.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the aim of abolishing wage labour and distributing by need, which favours machinery freeing time, though technology is not addressed.

multipolar-world.rationale: The Platform is internationalist and addresses neither power blocs nor world order; adherents would reject both great-power poles and no answer follows from its principles.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The Platform's critique of capitalism holds that the working class creates wealth and the exploiters appropriate it, in the labour-value tradition, though it never states the theory.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The Platform is internationalist and class-based, rejecting the nation-state as an instrument of the ruling class, so patriotism is treated as foreign to workers' struggle.

material-over-identity.rationale: Not stated directly; the Platform puts class struggle and workers' economic organisation first, but identity politics postdates it and this is inferred.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The Platform rejects any state, party dictatorship or transitional period and has production managed by workers' bodies, so a party-led market economy contradicts it.

missingStatements.text: An anarchist organisation should require its members to hold a common political programme and act on shared tactics.
missingStatements.rationale: The Platform's organisational principles of theoretical unity, tactical unity and collective responsibility define it against the synthesist model of loosely joined tendencies.

missingStatements.text: A revolutionary movement should act as the ideological guide of mass workers' organisations without taking state power.
missingStatements.rationale: The Platform has the General Union serve as pioneer and theoretical mentor of unions and peasant bodies while rejecting seizure of political power.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow to the Platform strand: it is "ideological guidance without power", which sits between vanguard-party (answered) and party-discipline-binding and is not a question other ideologies would split on independently.

notes: Contested by other anarchists: Volin, Berkman and Faure's synthesists called the Platform an anarchist party in disguise. Many answers on social and cultural questions are inferences since the 1926 text is silent.
